facts.fact_text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in the city of Malatya.

On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya, according to the Government's submissions.
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrators at the International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya on 8 March 2005 were carrying placards, flags and posters.

According to a report signed by eighteen police officers, at 2.00 p.m. on 8 March 2005, police received intelligence that a number of non-governmental organisations were planning to gather at the junction of Milli Egemenlik Street with a view to marching from there to the square outside the post office.
According to a report signed by eighteen police officers, the demonstrators began arriving at the junction of Milli Egemenlik Street at midday on 8 March 2005.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, a group comprising hundreds of police officers formed a cordon around the crowd.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
Police officers dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
The four arrested applicants were taken to a police station on 8 March 2005.
Later on 8 March 2005, the four arrested applicants were released from police custody.
According to the Government's submissions, police officers put a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles by force on 8 March 2005.

According to a report signed by eighteen police officers, police officers had to use force to arrest the applicants — with the exception of the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir — and five other demonstrators because they resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.

In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that in dispersing the unauthorised demonstration, the police officers had been impelled to resort to the use of force in order to apprehend the applicants because they had resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.

The criminal proceedings brought on 8 March 2005 against the four applicants and the five other arrested persons were for insulting the police officers and contravening the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicable legislation required no prior permission for the gathering.

A copy of the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004 was made available to the Court by the applicants.
In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, the Ministry urges police officers to respect certain rights and freedoms, including freedom of expression and assembly.

In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, the Ministry reminds police officers that rights and freedoms including freedom of expression and assembly can only be restricted in limited circumstances.

Ill-treatment of the detained women continued in the police vehicles after their arrest on 8 March 2005.
Male police officers started squeezing the arms and legs of the detained women inside the police vehicles.
The detained women told the police officers that the police officers had no right to behave as they were behaving.
The detained women asked for female police officers to accompany them in the police vehicles.
When the detained women told the police officers they had no right to behave as they were and asked for female police officers, the detained women were sworn at by the police officers.
The episode of ill-treatment in the police vehicles lasted for approximately twenty minutes.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the four applicants who had been hit by police officers had a number of injuries on their bodies.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the injuries sustained by the four applicants rendered them unable to work for periods of between one and three days.
The part of the video footage where the police officers used force and arrested the applicants does not feature in the footage submitted to the Court.
The video footage begins with police officers trying to persuade the demonstrators to leave their placards behind.
The video footage resumes with the demonstrators protesting against the use of force by the police officers and asking for their arrested friends to be released.

In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, police officers are urged to use their powers to promote the rights of civil society.

According to the doctor at the Malatya State Hospital, the injuries observed on the first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, on 10 March 2005 had been caused some thirty-six to forty-eight hours previously.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the demonstrators had tried to break the police cordon and march on 8 March 2005.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the police officers had not behaved in an arbitrary manner on 8 March 2005.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the use of force by the police officers on 8 March 2005 had not been excessive.
On 12 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor decided not to prosecute the police officers involved in the events of 8 March 2005.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, had been unable to recognise the police officer who had sprayed her with tear gas.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that the applicants had gathered in the area without having sought prior permission.

In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that in dispersing the unauthorised demonstration, the police officers had been impelled to resort to the use of force in order to apprehend the applicants because they had resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.
In his decision of 12 May 2005, the Malatya prosecutor stated that other than the applicants' unsubstantiated allegations, there was no evidence justifying the prosecution of the police officers.
The objection filed by the applicants against the Malatya prosecutor's decision not to prosecute the police officers was rejected by the Elazığ Assize Court on 28 July 2005.
On 2 June 2005 the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance acquitted the four applicants and the remaining defendants.
The Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance held on 2 June 2005 that there was no evidence to show that the four applicants had put up resistance against the police officers.
